positions.choice: Text only in page files; display = render(span) cut from page text; selector exact is a checked locator, never displayed; closed render-deletion list (B's).
positions.reason: Both plans agree; B's explicit render rule (only footnote markers removed, sigla kept unless span ends before) is more testable than mine.

positions.choice: Page file is the only Arabic text; display resolved from span; closed render rule deleting only footnote markers; tested render(span)==page slice minus markers.
positions.reason: Both plans agree; copy-and-check produced 414/727 failures. B's explicit render test closes the remaining gap.

positions.choice: Display = render(span) with B's closed, tested deletion list (footnote markers, intra-span breaks only); siglum stays or the span ends before it; book's ayah quotation shown as printed.
positions.reason: A 3.3/6.6 still renders a quoted ayah from the Ayah table inside a commentator's text; that substitutes a reading. B's render test makes 'resolved' provable.
positions.condition: A drops Ayah substitution and adopts B's render test.

positions.choice: Text only in page files; display = page slice at resolved span minus a closed, tested deletion list (footnote markers only); exact is a locator, never displayed.
positions.reason: Both plans agree; B's explicit render test (5a) is the piece that makes 'display is the source' provable rather than asserted.
positions.condition: Adopt B's render-equals-slice test in model:check.

positions.choice: B's Assertion (subject, predicate, value spans/object/parsed/classified, restsOn statements) replacing catalog; my Statement fields fold in; subject refs via Mention+Identification.
positions.reason: B separates what is shown from what was said, and its 'classified' value with span beside it names our reading honestly; mine conflated report wording and value.
positions.condition: Assertion entity references must still pass through Mention and Identification, not bare slugs.

positions.choice: A's Statement under a Report, about[] as Mention ids, predicate vocab; add B's parsed vs classified object split.
positions.reason: Routing every entity through Mention removes unrecorded identifications; Report gives speaker derivation. Plain Siyar claim costs ~report+statement+2 spans, acceptable.
positions.condition: Author-voice reports need a frame or heading span, not default.

positions.choice: B's Assertion/Statement split with parsed vs classified values, but subject and object must be Mention ids reached through Identification (A's rule).
positions.reason: B's Assertion.subject 'agent:az-zubayr' is an unrecorded identification by us. A's Mention-everywhere rule fixes it; B's parsed/classified split is the better value type.
positions.condition: Siyar plain claim cost stays about 6 records with heading identification explicit-in-text reviewed in bulk.

positions.choice: A's Statement with about[]/object as Mention ids plus Report voice; keep B's parsed/classified split for scalars and Statement.role for ADR 0011.
positions.reason: Routing every entity through a Mention makes each identification visible; ~6 records per plain Siyar value is acceptable if explicit-in-text identifications are bulk-reviewed.
positions.condition: Explicit-in-text identifications get bulk review tooling, not per-record clicks.

positions.choice: Speaker per statement with author basis span; Link.mode as span list with 1:1 modeKey from printed lemma; explicit Gap elements; enclosure separate from chain; anonymous = unidentified mention.
positions.reason: Gap elements and enclosure model muallaq, mursal and 'qala Ibn Sa'd' better than my booleans; 1:1 key beats my closed vocabulary with jazm/tamrid as derived view.
positions.condition: Keep jazm/tamrid as a documented derived view, never replacing modeKey on edges.

positions.choice: A's Report/Chain/Link with modeSpans[] and gapBefore, vocab extended to person/number 1:1 and jazm/tamrid class; reported-anonymous voice for وقيل.
positions.reason: A's vocabulary is richer and covers tamrid; B's Gap element equals gapBefore. No edge across a gap either way.
positions.condition: Unmapped printed formula fails check instead of 'unspecified'.

positions.choice: B's modeKey 1:1 with printed lemma+person/number, Gap elements anywhere (ta'liq, mursal, balagha), enclosedBy; add A's derived jazm/tamrid class, Edition.riwayah and reported-anonymous voice.
positions.reason: A's gapBefore cannot express a mursal's missing tail; A's codes miss person/number for samia. B lacks riwayah of the book and the tamrid class.
positions.condition: Abbreviated formulas (ثنا، نا، أنا) map to their full key with the abbreviation span kept.

positions.choice: B's Chain of (Link|Gap) elements and lemma+person modeKey; add A's jazm/tamrid class, Unit layer, Edition.riwayah and reported-anonymous voice.
positions.reason: A Gap element prevents false edges more robustly than A's gapBefore flag; A's tamrid class and riwayah chain capture distinctions B lacks.
positions.condition: modeKey stays 1:1 with printed form; classes are derived.

positions.choice: Global Agent per person; Identification with admissible basis roles (editor note, rijal entry, same-work explicit incl. heading); mention's own span never a basis; segment identifications reused per work.
positions.reason: Stricter than my namaq-authored basis, which let our opinion in; segment reuse makes review cost tractable.
positions.condition: Competing sourced identifications all DISPUTED; Namaq never picks.

positions.choice: Global Entity, Mention everywhere (A); basis roles excluding mention's own span except heading-subject (B); chain-segment identification reuse with listed applications (B).
positions.reason: A's explicit-in-text is fine for headings but not ambiguous isnad names; reuse makes Bukhari affordable without blind approval.
positions.condition: Ambiguous isnad names never identified on explicit-in-text.

positions.choice: Global entity; Identification needs a basis span other than the mention itself (EDITOR_NOTE, RIJAL_ENTRY, SAME_WORK_EXPLICIT); no basis means unidentified text, no node; reuse per chain segment within a work.
positions.reason: A's 'namaq-authored' identifications shown as labelled edges are our opinion on hadith narrators. B's honest unidentified state meets the Prophetic standard.

positions.choice: Global entity, Mention, Identification with basis; basis never the mention's own span; segment-level reuse (A's mention+neighbour pair); edges only from reviewed identifications.
positions.reason: A shows namaq-authored unreviewed identifications as edges with a label; for narrators of Prophetic hadith that publishes our opinion as a chain. Visibility as text, edges after review.
positions.condition: Unreviewed identifications visible as text with label, never as graph edges.

positions.choice: Report/Tradition groups unmerged wordings with basis spans or NAMAQ basis shown as 'grouped by Namaq'.
positions.reason: Plans agree; labelled Namaq grouping is honest and useful.
positions.condition: Owner may forbid NAMAQ basis (open question).

positions.choice: Tradition/Report grouping over unmerged wordings, membership with basis; namaq-authored grouping allowed but labelled 'grouped by Namaq'.
positions.reason: Both reject merged texts; labelling keeps our judgment visible rather than forbidding useful grouping.
positions.condition: Owner may forbid Namaq grouping for hadith (open question).

positions.reason: Both refuse merging and label Namaq groupings. Grouping marfu' hadith on our word implies a judgment about sameness of the Prophet's words.
positions.condition: Owner may relax for hadith via Q3/Q9.

positions.choice: A's Tradition + Membership with basis (same-origin-and-matn, editor-takhrij, atraf-index, namaq-authored), never merging wordings; namaq-authored labelled in UI.
positions.reason: Separating Tradition from Report and typing the basis is clearer than B's Report-of-Statements; both refuse merged text.
positions.condition: Owner decides whether namaq-authored groupings may publish.

positions.choice: Per-record contentHash including hash of rendered text and witness of every reached span; publish = owner publishes set of record hashes; edit lapses that record only.
positions.reason: Same as mine in effect; hashing rendered text catches witness switches too.

positions.choice: Per-record publication; revision hash over record fields plus rendered text of named spans and transcription id; reanchor with same text lapses nothing.
positions.reason: Both converge after review; includes witness so a transcription switch lapses affected records.

positions.choice: Per-record publication with minted ids; revision hash = record fields + sha256(rendered text) + witness id of each span (B); only the owner runs publish per change set (A).
positions.reason: B's hash catches displayed text moving; A's owner-run publish keeps the AGENTS.md gate. Together nothing lapses en masse except where display truly moved.

positions.choice: Per-record publication; hash = record + sha256(render(span)) + witness id for every span reached; reanchor with identical rendered text keeps publication.
positions.reason: A hashes only exact; a re-split or witness switch can change displayed text under a published hash. B's hash catches it while still surviving pure re-anchors.
positions.condition: Only if A shows display text cannot change while exact is unchanged.

positions.choice: data/works (works, editions, witnesses), sources per witness, records per work-unit (A's layout) not per batch; PG and Neo4j derived; NARRATED_FROM edges from reviewed identifications, never across Gap.
positions.reason: Batches are a work-process grouping, not a source structure; files per tarjama/hadith map to the book and avoid batch folders recurring.
positions.condition: Accept B's per-batch folders if owner prefers PR-sized units.

positions.reason: Unit files follow the book's structure and scale to Bukhari better than subject batches; separating isnad edges keeps the people graph readable.
positions.condition: Change sets list record ids for publication, replacing batch.json approval.

positions.choice: A's layout (data/works/<work>/units, data/entities) with change sets as PRs; B's Neo4j rule: NARRATED_FROM only from reviewed identifications, never across a Gap, modeKey+span ids on edge.
positions.reason: Unit-per-file follows the book's structure for hadith and tafsir; batches are a work-process artefact. Edges from unreviewed identifications contradict the hadith standard.
positions.condition: An ADR supersedes 0010's layout.

positions.choice: Files per Unit under data/works and data/entities; PostgreSQL and Neo4j derived; catalog/batches retired; seeds archived; NARRATED_FROM in separate isnad view, excluded from centrality.
positions.reason: Unit-shaped files match how sources are read and reviewed; A's archive keeps old values inspectable; separating isnad edges protects the companion graph layout.
positions.condition: B's Gloss directory added for English names.

E2 Arabic search normalisation (diacritic-insensitive) over rendered spans
E3 How quiz questions cite statements that later lapse or change
E4 Reviewer independence: the owner is the only reviewer; who is a hadith-qualified reviewer and how their review is recorded distinctly
E5 Shamela text is a transcription: no check against printed page images, so a host typo or host-inserted honorific becomes exact
E6 Re-fetched tashkeel corrections on a published Prophetic matn: policy; normalisation version bumps and what re-resolves or lapses
E7 Abbreviated transmission formulas (ثنا، نا، أنا، ثني) mapped to mode keys; idraj and narrator-doubt words (أَوْ قَالَ، أَحْسِبُهُ) inside a matn span
E8 Taqti and ikhtisar: a report cut across chapters, partial wordings within one report
E9 Editor takhrij footnotes (al-Arna'ut) as gradings with the editor as speaker; sigla such as (ع) as statements
E10 Shared chain segments repeated across hadiths: drift of duplicated identifications
E11 Qira'at variants in the Ayah table; the rijal work chosen as identification basis and its ingestion order
E12 Performance of resolving spans for ~200k records; projection tests for disputed graph edges
